atque inde eas mihi absurditates impegerit, a quibus alienissimus sum. In

dulgent adfectibus. Male cuncta ministrat Impetus. Ego vero uti credo me
non esse ἀναμάρτητον, ita meas caespitationes nolim obesse veritati. Quod pas-
sim exprobrat candoris defectum, id nescio quomodo a quoquam mortalium aliter
refutari possit, nisi videnti protestatione sinceritatis, illiusque ipso facto de-
monstratione ubi quis convincitur erroris. De animo enim judicare illius est qui
solus renes ac corda scrutatur. Abdita mentium caelesti menti reservanda:
nec pectoris fibrae pulsandae cuiquam & referandae, nisi qui eas fecit. Profi-
teor autem nihil a me cuiquam attributum esse, nisi quod ab ipso ita dictum
scriptumve existimavi: Si mentem cujusquam male expressero, non data id
factum esse opera, sed & ἀλληλίαν; quam monitus ita corrigam, nulla ut
querela remaneat materia. Sponte offero
Spongiam, aberrantis quae medicina stili est.
Id unum obtestatus, ut eodem & alii agant candore, neq; quaesitis verborum

Tu, Lector, quisquis pius, peritus, atque extra partes positus es, judica: Deumque

page.notes: The text is set in italic, with the words "Summa Theologiae Christianae" in roman. The Greek words are printed in Greek letters; the transcription of the Greek in the body ("ἐγχειρήσεως", "ἀναμάρτητον", "ἀλληλίαν") and of the motto line is uncertain at the letter level and should be checked. The small block at the foot is in smaller type; it was read as one block. The word "Valde" at the right may be a catchword or a signature, and is given as a catchword. "i<sup>l</sup>." is a superscript mark and is uncertain. Possible printing errors such as "creem" and "Lector" were left as printed.
